[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Window Functions and Rolling Operations in Pandas"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Window functions and rolling operations are essential tools for time-series analysis and data preprocessing in Python's Pandas library. They allow you to compute statistics across a sliding or expanding window of data points."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before diving into rolling operations, ensure you have Pandas installed. We will start by importing Pandas and creating a sample DataFrame containing time-series data."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)
dates = pd.date_range('2023-01-01', periods=10)
df = pd.DataFrame({'value': np.random.randint(10, 100, size=10)}, index=dates)
print(df)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Rolling Window Calculations"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The rolling() method provides rolling window calculations. You specify the window size using the 'window' parameter, and then chain an aggregation method such as mean(), sum(), or std()."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Calculate a 3-period rolling mean
df['rolling_mean'] = df['value'].rolling(window=3).mean()
print(df)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Expanding Window Calculations"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Unlike rolling windows which have a fixed size, expanding windows include all historical data up to the current point. This is useful for calculating cumulative statistics like cumulative sums or expanding averages."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Calculate expanding maximum
df['expanding_max'] = df['value'].expanding().max()
print(df)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Takeaways"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use df['col'].rolling(window=n) for moving averages and sliding window metrics."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use df['col'].expanding() to include all preceding rows in the calculation."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always handle NaN values generated at the beginning of rolling and expanding operations appropriately."}]
